title: Good value, boring selection, slightly deceptive display pics
text:
Here's my review of the July K-Glow Box. This is what's inside:

*Leaders - What Happened Last Night? Glowing Facial Mist
*Jeju:en Hyaluron Hydrogel Lip Patches
*Jeju:en Propolis Cream
*BetterSkin Premium Volcanic Ash & Botanical Fermentation Detoxing Sheet Mask
*Medius Ampoule Synergy - Moisture Plus
*Mediheal Cica: Ming Mask
*NoHj Healing Mask Pack Lustre

First off, I gotta say the display image for the K-Glow box is deceptive... It shows 3 full size items, a speciality item, and FIVE masks. Except the description itself says 3 full size items, 3 masks, and 1 specialty item... And I got 3 full size items and 4 masks (NO specialty item).

Here's my unpopular opinion on k beauty skincare.. Exoticism is a great marketing tool; in the past it was all about those exotic French women with their beauty secrets, and skincare brands with French names sold as luxury items. Now it's all about Korean beauty. In reality, a lot of these masks and creams are really just basic drugstore quality products in Korea, there's anything better about a Leaders face mist than something you could pick up at your local drugstore.

I'm Asian, I've lived in Asia. I've gone shopping in Myeongdong a couple times, and Facetory sells brands like Nature Republic masks at a 1000% markup (compared to what you'd pay for a pack of masks). Paying more for a foreign products doesn't mean it's inherently superior. I'd pay extra for stuff I can't find equivalents of here, but a basic cream and a face mist was a boring letdown considering I might as well just pick some up at the store five minutes from my house. If I'm paying for foreign products, I'd like stuff I can't easily find here, like k beauty serums or unique ingredients like slug.

To be clear: the K-Glow box is a good value, but the selection was a little boring--stuff you can easily find local equivalents of. I don't need a K beauty box for that, and
label: positive
